How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing through SIA, I applied for multiple apartments and did not get my first priority at all. But I was very happy in the end.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I bought a bike at KSR sykkel, but you could also get a bus pass on the akt-billet app. I lived at Lund Torv, so about 15 minutes on the bike away from campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately not all classes where for exchange students, but there was some classes that I liked.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *

questions.answer: Go on adventures with other exchange students and attend the things plan by the ESN.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy enough. Grocery stores being closed on Sunday was a bit annoying.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports team.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: A lot of nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Not about the destination but about exchange. Make friends and try hard in the beginning - ask everyone that seem sweet to be a part of your group. Bring things that will make you happy about home - I had photos, a football scarf, a teddy bear. Make frequent calls home - just to chat, when you get home you will feel that everything is the same just you changed a bit.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a friend that lives close to you. I lived off campus and did not click to well with my roommate. So having someone to shop and study and just in general hangout with is much needed, because it can easily feel like you are away from the "party" at campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends and going on adventures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Roommate troubles to be honest.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
